headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 18 of the 31 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in Northern Vermont and White Mountains. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Temperatures becoming warmer heading into November.
A cold front will move through the Northeast late this week bringing breezes and periods of rain possibly Thursday through the weekend.

ALY.excerpt: ) Mostly dry weather is expected through Wednesday, with increasing chances for rain later in the week. Above normal temperatures are expected through the upcoming week.

GYX.excerpt: Temperatures will average above normal through the middle of the week with mostly dry weather. Precipitation chances increase towards the end of the week.

BUF.excerpt:
) Warmer today and dry through Monday.
) A chance of showers Tuesday. Well above normal temperatures expected for much of the upcoming work week.

PHI.excerpt:
Some areas of frost this morning and again tonight. Otherwise, generally tranquil weather is expected to prevail through the middle portion of next week.
Rain is expected to return late next week.

CTP.excerpt: ) Our lengthy run of dry and mild weather continues until the second half of the week.

RLX.excerpt: ) Much of the area should remain dry into early next week, then a system brings widespread precipitation chances mid to late week.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:21}} to {{t:55}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Burke gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 9).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Sunday 1:56 AM: "Temperatures becoming warmer heading into November."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.
